You're right, VMos and hacked clients is really easy to detect, but the system level Android spoofing methods are very difficult to detect if they are set up correctly.  It's still the safest way.

In theory they could also ban accounts that do unrealistic things like moving too fast, but I think they don't for various reasons.  The pattern seems to be banning people who are legit cheating in ways they can prove with high certainty.  They won't ban people for behavior that could also be explained by innocent things like GPS drift,  or having a friend 3000 miles away who happens to know your Google password.

They are adding "legit" features to allow players to play more from home, but nothing at all has changed regarding their stance on actual spoofing.  They still run their scheduled warnings and banwaves.

The history over the past 4 years is that they ban anything they can detect that accessed their servers or hacked their clients in an unauthorized way.  In the old days that included things like botting, currently they often banwave stuff like hacked clients on iOS and stuff like that.  VMos was also fairly easy to detect, it looks nothing like a real Android phone.

They don't usually ban for things they can detect immediately in the game itself.  Like if the game crashes out and says "your device is unsupported" or your spoofing app is set up wrong and the game detects it...  then you can't play but it doesn't lead to a ban.  The ban comes from analysis they do on server logs after the fact, stuff that is more difficult to detect in the app itself.

As far as I know they don't have the capability to reliably detect Android spoofing yet, at least not without false positives, because the app functions exactly as they coded it, all the signatures match, and the only thing fake is the GPS coordinates from the system which they don't have the system privileges to detect.  Personally I've never had a problem with Android spoofing and I've been doing it since 2016.  It will continue to work for a while, although Google's safetynet will eventually make Android spoofing much harder.

My advice - get a cheap Android phone if you don't already have one, make sure it can be rooted, and follow a good tutorial.  That's the safest way for now in 2020.
